role.altitude: The preschool special education teacher keeps deciding objectives, choosing activities, supervising, presenting and agreeing programs with colleagues; collecting results by hand, writing outlines and adapted materials from scratch, chasing consent slips and hunting for clips shrink.
skills_to_grow: Checking drafted objectives against the curriculum goals
Adapting drafted materials to each child
role.ambitious_version: A teacher who spends preparation time on adapting for individual children rather than on typing outlines.

tasks.short: Gather results and feedback on the current program, collaborate with other teachers or administrators to evaluate and revise preschool programs, write the revised sections and share them for final agreement.

steps.what: Teacher gathers goal results and feedback on the current program
Teacher collaborates with other teachers and administrators to evaluate and revise preschool programs
Teacher writes the revised program sections

loop.input: The agreed revisions and the current program text.
loop.output: Draft revised sections in the program template.
loop.check: Each objective must map to a core goal code; the teacher reads each drafted section against the points the team agreed and rewrites anything that says more or other than was agreed.
loop.stop: The teacher shares the sections, or writes them by hand after two redrafts.
loop.why_not_simpler: Program text must follow what was agreed in the meeting.

steps.what: Teacher shares the revised program for comments and final agreement

tasks.design: A group overview in the pupil record shows goal attainment per program area, so results are not tallied by hand. Evaluating and agreeing revisions stay in the team meeting. A drafting step writes the revised sections from the agreed points, each objective mapped to a core goal code, and the revised text is shared as one document with comments instead of mailed versions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Results were tallied by hand and versions mailed around.
tasks.enabler_now: Goal tracking in pupil records, shared documents and drafting checked against goal codes.
tasks.still_hard: Colleagues with different views on what works.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which change the team will actually carry out.

ambition.what: Review the program each term instead of each year.

tasks.altitude: Less tallying and writing; the discussion stays.

evidence.claim: A pupil record system tracks learning goals and support plans.

assumptions: Boundary: evaluating and revising the group program; modifying the curriculum for individual disabilities (task 19074) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s1: goals tracked per child in the pupil record by the teachers.
The team discussion keeps its full time.
research_questions: Do revisions use outcome data more often?

incremental.description: Teacher keeps the program template and goal codes current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: small revisions, so the overview and draft help little and s1 keeps 80 and s3 keeps 90 (12.2); high: full yearly programme reviews (21.9).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Look up curriculum goals, prepare objectives and outlines for courses of study, prepare materials such as worksheets, picture cards and adapted texts, and check the final materials fit the children.

steps.what: Teacher looks up the curriculum goals for the period
Teacher prepares objectives and outlines for courses of study following curriculum guidelines

loop.input: The goals for the period and the teacher's notes on the group.
loop.output: Draft objectives and an outline of weekly themes.
loop.check: Each objective must map to a curriculum goal code; the teacher reads each objective against the goal's meaning and the group notes and rewrites objectives that do not fit the children.
loop.stop: The teacher keeps the outline, or writes it by hand after two redrafts.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each group needs a different sequence and pace.

steps.what: Teacher prepares materials: worksheets, picture cards and adapted texts

loop.input: Existing materials and texts from the school's library.
loop.output: Versions at a simpler level, with pictograms where chosen.
loop.check: The teacher reads every adapted text and picture card before use.
loop.stop: One adaptation per material; otherwise the teacher adapts by hand.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each child needs a different level of language and support.

steps.what: Teacher checks the final materials fit the children

tasks.design: The curriculum goals sit as a fixed list in the planning tool. A drafting step writes objectives and a weekly outline from the goals and the teacher's notes on the group, each objective mapped to a goal code. A lesson editor rewrites existing texts at a simpler level and adds pictograms where chosen. The teacher reads and adapts everything and checks the final materials against the children.
tasks.previous_blocker: Outlines and adapted materials were written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Lesson editors that rewrite text at another level and drafting checked against goal codes.
tasks.still_hard: Children who need materials no tool produces, such as tactile cards.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing what will hold this child's attention.
tasks.altitude: Less writing; adapting to children stays.

reach.learn: Whether shared adapted materials save their time too.

evidence.claim: A lesson editor rewrites text at another level, summarises and translates.
In a randomised trial a lesson assistant cut weekly preparation from 3.3 to 2.5 hours, but covered 7% of lessons and use declined.

assumptions: Boundary: preparing objectives, outlines and materials; modifying the curriculum for individual disabilities (task 19074) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s3: the school's material library holds the texts to adapt.
Checking keeps its full time; uptake may stay low, as in the trial.
unknowns: How often teachers will use the drafting tools.
research_questions: Does preparation time fall without poorer materials?

already_counted.description: Teacher corrects drafted objectives and adapted texts.

incremental.description: Teacher keeps the material library tidy.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: low uptake, as in the trial, so s2 and s3 keep 90 (14.0); high: regular use for outlines and adapted texts (28.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan experiential learning activities, arrange transport, venue and helpers, collect parent consent and medical details, and supervise class projects, field trips or demonstrations.

steps.what: Teacher plans the experiential learning activity: goals, place and program
Teacher prepares the transport, venue and helper arrangements: by phone and e-mail today, from the standard trip checklist with usual transport and venues after the change
Teacher checks the booking requests before they go: date, times, number of children and helpers, and access needs
Teacher sends the checked booking requests to the transport company and venue
Teacher prepares the consent and medical details request in the parent app
Teacher checks the consent request before it goes: date, place, programme and the medical questions
Teacher sends the checked consent request to the parents in the parent app
Parents give consent and medical details in the parent app
Teacher collects parent consent forms and medical details
Teacher supervises the class project, field trip or demonstration

tasks.design: A standard trip checklist with the school's usual transport and venues shortens arranging; the teacher checks the booking requests and sends them once. The teacher checks the consent request and sends it once; parents give consent and update medical details in the parent app, and the teacher sees who is missing instead of chasing paper slips; medical details are visible only to the staff on the trip. Planning and supervising stay fully with the teacher.

approvals.approved_version: The booking requests with date, times, number of children and helpers and access needs exactly as checked by the teacher in s2b, sent once to the named transport company and venue; any change needs a new check.

The consent request with date, place, programme and medical questions exactly as checked by the teacher in s4b, sent once to the parents of the children on the trip in the parent app; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Paper consent slips went missing and had to be chased.
tasks.still_hard: Children whose needs change on the day.
tasks.human_edge: Keeping every child safe in an unfamiliar place.
tasks.altitude: Less chasing; planning and supervising stay.

reach.learn: Whether consent is complete before the day.

evidence.claim: A pupil record system offers a parent app.
Parents must consent to the school's rules on pupil data.

assumptions: Boundary: planning and supervising experiential activities; recreational games (task 19077) are a sibling task.
Input contract for s4: parents use the parent app, about 85% of them; the rest return paper slips; s4 is priced at that share.
Parents' time in the app is shown in s3 at share 1 and is about what a paper slip took. The checks and sends of bookings and the consent request keep their full time.
Planning and supervising keep their full time.
research_questions: Do trips start with complete consent more often?

incremental.description: Teacher keeps the trip checklist and usual venues current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few trips to the usual venues and fewer parents on the app, so s2 keeps 80 and s4 keeps 60 (5.6); high: about 85% of parents on the app as assumed (10.4).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Find or make audio-visual and interactive material, set up the equipment, and present information in audio-visual or interactive formats to the children.

steps.what: Teacher finds or makes audio-visual and interactive material
Teacher sets up the screen, sound and interactive equipment
Teacher presents information in audio-visual or interactive formats and engages the children

tasks.design: A shared library of checked clips and interactive lessons, tagged by theme and level, replaces searching the internet for each lesson, and a lesson editor lets the teacher adapt an existing interactive lesson. Setting up and presenting stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Suitable clips were searched for and checked lesson by lesson.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared clip libraries and lesson editors.
tasks.still_hard: Children who are overstimulated by screens.
tasks.human_edge: Pausing at the right moment to let a child respond.

evidence.claim: A lesson editor rewrites, summarises and translates lesson text.

assumptions: Boundary: presenting with media; preparing course materials (task 19080) is a sibling task.
Setting up and presenting keep their full time.

incremental.description: Teacher adds checked clips to the shared library.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small library with few lessons at the right level, so s1 keeps 85 (4.2); high: a well-tagged shared library (11.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
